config.notes: Re-run the release-prep pipeline for 0.0.11 after the medterm4ds PyPI migration (commit bd5d7ded). Prior campaign archived under archive/20260810-01/. Pipeline is sequential (no evolution loop): code_review -> pre_release -> docs_audit -> benchmarks -> scribe. Each workflow runs once. Discovery: today's commit changed pyproject.toml [terminology] extra to declare medterm4ds>=0.0.1, removed dead legacy import fallbacks (engines.local_duckdb, apps.fhir_api_helpers) from in_process_adapter, dropped the unsupported 'categories' kwarg from NotesPipelineConfig (it never worked against published medterm4ds.extract), and rewrote the in_process_adapter test stub to mirror the canonical PyPI surface. 1562 unit tests pass; all 4 medterm4ds integration phases pass against live PyPI medterm4ds 0.0.1. Release Engineer artifact gate required per ROLE_INITIALIZER section 2 notes - the pipeline includes pre_release which owns that gate natively. Focus areas per USER_DIRECTIVES: (1) conformance run_all.py must remain 100%; (2) full pytest suite must pass; (3) for every DuckDB-backed surface, compare native C++ extension vs forced Python fallback; (4) perf benchmarks vs prior baseline, scaling cliffs/memory spikes/unexplained regressions are blockers; (5) release/package/import checks for 0.0.11.

issues.evidence: docs/architecture/plans/FEATURE_MEDTERM4DS_PHASE4_NER.md:40-67 still documents `categories: list[str] | None = None` as part of the medterm4ds.extract contract and lists `categories=None (all)` as a NotesPipelineConfig default. Per the commit message the published PyPI medterm4ds 0.0.1 wheel does NOT accept `categories`. The code now correctly omits it but the FDD still advertises the kwarg, which will mislead anyone implementing against the FDD as the source of truth. Recommended fix: update lines 40-67 to reflect the actual published medterm4ds.extract signature (format, mode, min_grade, include_negated/uncertain/historical). Note: this is primarily a docs_audit-owned artifact but flagged here because the commit explicitly cites the FDD as the spec reference (notes_pipeline.py:13).
issues.fix: Rewrote the 'medterm4ds.extract contract' block in FEATURE_MEDTERM4DS_PHASE4_NER.md to enumerate the actual published PyPI medterm4ds 0.0.1 signature: extract(text, *, format, ner_labels, result_types, mode, min_grade, include_negated, include_uncertain, include_historical). Removed the `categories: list[str] | None = None` parameter from the signature and removed `categories=None (all)` from the NotesPipelineConfig defaults list. Added a re-release note block (dated 2026-08-10) explaining that the pre-PyPI draft listed `categories` and that anchor-type filtering is done via `result_types`. Cross-checked against fhir4ds/cql/loader/notes_pipeline.py:_extract_kwargs() which sends only format/mode/min_grade/include_negated/include_uncertain/include_historical.

issues.evidence: fhir4ds-private/docs/notebooks/viewdef.ipynb (untracked, internal playground) cell 4 raises CatalogException 'Table with name resources does not exist!' when executed. The notebook creates a 'patients' table but the ViewDefinition targets resource 'Patient' which generates SQL referencing the default 'resources' table. Pre-existing issue unrelated to the 0.0.11 re-release or the medterm4ds PyPI migration. The canonical public docs/notebooks/viewdef.ipynb executes cleanly (verified via jupyter nbconvert --to notebook --execute, zero cell errors). Filed for completeness only; not a blocker because (a) the private notebooks directory is not tracked by git, (b) it is not published to the website, (c) the public notebook is clean. Recommended fix (deferred): either drop the notebook or change `connection.execute('CREATE TABLE patients ...')` to use the shared 'resources' table name.
